target_customer: Employers moving to ICHRA, families and individuals choosing plans, and clinics handling prior authorizations and denial appeals
problem: People choose health plans by sticker premium rather than full-year cost, and clinics lose time and revenue to prior authorizations and denials. Insurf prices plans by county and drafts source-cited appeals.
business_model: B2B and B2C health insurance software; product lines Surely (plan cost engine) and Inveto (clinic appeals), pricing not found
product_category: Health insurance decision and prior authorization software

founders.name: Bryan Chung
education: Brown University (met co-founder at orientation per launch post)
founders.background_notes: Bio lists international physics and CS competition placements, two IEEE publications, USACO Platinum, research at Cambridge, Brown, CMU, RIT and UCSC.

founders.name: Chang Lu
education: Brown University, BS/MD program, neuroscience and economics
founders.background_notes: Launch post says he was accepted to medical school at 17 and worked a pharmacy counter.

competitors.name: Thatch
competitors.what: ICHRA administration platform for small employers
competitors.funding_then: described as best funded all-in-one in a 2026 roundup

competitors.name: Zorro
competitors.what: Broker-first ICHRA platform with AI plan selection support

competitors.name: Counterforce Health
competitors.what: Nonprofit AI that writes insurance denial appeal letters
competitors.traction_then: claimed 70 percent reversal rate on a third-party listing, unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Pricing every county plan over a full usage year and building version-pinned, cited appeal packets needs data pipelines over messy plan documents and clinical records. Standard engineering with some hard data work.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded ICHRA and AI appeals players exist. A claimed data collection loop from clinics into the Surely model could compound, but it is early and unverified.

market_need_then: The launch post cites a 2028 shift away from auto-renewing plans and growth of ICHRA; denial rates and appeal overturn rates (company cites 80.7 percent for appealed Medicare Advantage denials, methodology not found) drive clinic demand.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, confident and numbers focused ('priced to the dollar'), with careful disclaimers on projections

brand_strength.rationale: No independent press about the brand; confusable with Insurify, Surest and similar names in search results.

outcome_analysis: Insurf is a Summer 2026 company with two founders and no disclosed revenue or verified funding. It pairs an employer and consumer plan pricing model with a clinic appeals tool that it says is live in Texas, Georgia and California. Outcome is open; the main risks are crowded ICHRA and AI appeals markets and thin independent evidence.
notes: Unverified funding: CB Insights lists a $500K convertible note with Y Combinator only, and Dealroom lists a $125K seed; the two conflict and neither is a primary source, so no round is recorded. Sources disagree on HQ (Providence per YC, San Francisco or Atlanta elsewhere) and team size. Chang Lu is called CEO by an aggregator but the YC page lists both as co-founders.
